issues.legal_issue: A transfer of land made after publication of an acquisition notification does not bind the acquiring State.
material_facts: An acquisition notification was published before the original owner transferred the properties to the claimants.
A declaration under the acquisition law was published after the transfers.
issues.conclusion: The post-notification transfers were void as against the State and did not bind it.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, a transfer made after publication of the acquisition notification is void as against the State. The Court also noted the subsequent declaration under Section 6. No earlier cases were relied upon.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The dispute concerns land acquired through a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.notification_preceded_transfer: An acquisition notification was published before the owner transferred the land.

issues.definition: When an acquisition proceeding is involved and the notification preceded the transfer, the transfer does not bind the acquiring State.

issues.legal_issue: Taking possession after an award completes the acquisition and vests the land free of encumbrances, and delivery to the beneficiary gives it ownership.
material_facts: An award was made following notices to the interested persons.
An officer took possession, recording it in a panchanama signed by a witness.
The acquired land was handed over to the beneficiary society.
issues.conclusion: Possession was validly taken and handed over; the State acquired the land free of encumbrances, and the beneficiary society became its absolute owner.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, after possession is taken following the award, the land vests in the State free from all encumbrances. The Court stated that possession may be taken through the usual mode of an officer preparing a panchanama signed by a witness, and that such possession is complete and conclusive. On handover, the beneficiary became absolute owner. No earlier cases were relied upon.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and award_made and possession_recorded_by_officer_in_witnessed_panchanama and acquired_land_delivered_to_beneficiary

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The land is the subject of a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.award_made: An award was made in the acquisition proceeding.
predicates.possession_recorded_by_officer_in_witnes: An officer took possession and recorded it in a panchanama signed by a witness.
predicates.acquired_land_delivered_to_beneficiary: The acquired land was handed over to the person or entity for whose benefit it was acquired.

issues.definition: In an acquisition proceeding, when an award has been made, possession is recorded in a witnessed panchanama, and the acquired land is delivered to the beneficiary, the land vests free of encumbrances and the beneficiary becomes its absolute owner.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant cannot acquire title to acquired land by adverse possession without pleading and proving the required hostile, known, acquiesced-in, and uninterrupted possession after possession has been taken and delivered.
material_facts: The claimants relied on adverse possession to assert title to land that had been acquired and delivered to the beneficiary.

They did not plead and prove that, after delivery of possession, they asserted their own right to the beneficiary's knowledge, that the beneficiary acquiesced, and that their possession was uninterrupted and nec vi, nec clam, nec precario.
issues.conclusion: The claimants acquired no title by adverse possession.
issues.legal_principle: A claim of adverse possession requires pleading and proof that, after possession has been taken and handed over, the claimant asserted a right hostile to the owner to the owner's knowledge, the owner acquiesced, and possession remained uninterrupted, nec vi, nec clam, nec precario. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this principle.

rule.if: acquisition_title_dispute and adverse_possession_claim and not (post_delivery_hostile_assertion_proved and owner's_knowledge_and_acquiescence_proved and uninterrupted_nec_vi_nec_clam_nec_precario_possession_proved)

predicates.acquisition_title_dispute: The dispute concerns a claim to land after possession has been taken in an acquisition proceeding and delivered to its beneficiary.
predicates.adverse_possession_claim: A claimant asserts that possession of the land has given them title by adverse possession.
predicates.post_delivery_hostile_assertion_proved: The claimant pleaded and proved that, after delivery of possession, they asserted their own right hostile to the owner.
predicates.owner's_knowledge_and_acquiescence_prove: The claimant pleaded and proved that the owner knew of the hostile assertion and acquiesced in it.
predicates.uninterrupted_nec_vi_nec_clam_nec_precar: The claimant pleaded and proved uninterrupted possession that was not by force, in secrecy, or by permission.

issues.definition: In a dispute over acquired land, an adverse-possession claim does not establish title when the claimant has not pleaded and proved all the stated facts about hostile assertion, the owner's knowledge and acquiescence, and uninterrupted possession.
